relatedLines.stakeHasTheGuard: src/StableStaker.sol:301 (require(credited > 0) — asymmetry suggests oversight, not design)

findings.description: Phantom zero-amount staker permanently bricks finalizeAndReset, freezing the pool in Migrating forever. depositFor (onlyMigrator) pulls amount > 0 but credits strategy-booked principal; a haircutting market strategy can book credited == 0 for a dust redeposit. Unlike stake(), depositFor has no require(credited > 0) and unconditionally adds the user to _stakers, creating a staker with amount == 0. No path can ever remove them: withdraw/emergencyWithdraw require amount > 0; _exitPosition (used by batchMigrate AND userMigrate) early-returns on amt == 0 WITHOUT removing from the set; while Migrating, depositFor is blocked (requires Active) so the position cannot be topped up to heal. finalizeAndReset then reverts 'stakers remain' forever — the pool slot is permanently stuck in Migrating, which is precisely the 'frozen forever / redeploy required' limitation story-009's finalizeAndReset was introduced to remove. All real principal can still exit via userMigrate/batchMigrate (no direct fund loss), but the token can never be revived: availability impact -> potential-medium under C4.
findings.confidenceRationale: All code signatures verified by reading the source (guard asymmetry, early return, set gate). Reaching credited == 0 requires the NEW staker to have a haircutting strategy wired and a dust-sized per-user credit (small min(R,P)/P credits from an underwater old pool make dust redeposits realistic in exactly the migration flow depositFor exists for). Trigger plausibility, not mechanism, is the open question — Tier-2/PoC should confirm a real strategy books 0 on dust.
matchedSignatures: uint256 credited = _routeDeposit(token, received); (depositFor, no credited > 0 check)

manualReview.description: Dust-stake grief of the empty-pool gate. The new require(totalStaked == 0) (line 228) is permissionlessly flippable: any 1-wei stake makes the gate fail. Two windows: (a) revival — between finalizeAndReset (pool returns to Active, idle-hold) and the owner's setYieldStrategy, a front-running 1-wei staker forces the owner to run an ENTIRE new terminal-migration cycle (initiateMigration -> eject -> finalizeAndReset) just to wire the strategy; (b) first adoption — a brand-new pool (addToken -> users stake) can never adopt a strategy without the full migration cycle once anyone has staked. Maps to the TWO-STEP-COMMIT-WINDOW vulnerableWhen 'a third party can force re-arm/reset the pending commit'.
manualReview.confidenceRationale: Mechanism confirmed, but a documented procedural mitigation exists: stake is whenNotPaused while finalizeAndReset and setYieldStrategy are deliberately pause-tolerant, and the finalizeAndReset natspec + CLAUDE.md prescribe wrapping revival in pause/unpause. The hazard is therefore an owner FOOTGUN (operator who skips the pause), and the warning is written down — leaning 'obvious -> trusted' under Law 3, but the cost asymmetry (1 wei vs a full migration cycle) is surprising enough to merit a human call. (b) first-adoption is intentional story-010 design per the updated CLAUDE.md (Law 2 faithful).
presentMitigations: stake() is whenNotPaused; setYieldStrategy/finalizeAndReset work while paused
finalizeAndReset natspec: 'recommended revival runbook wraps the reconfiguration in pause/unpause'
story-010 docs (CLAUDE.md) document the empty-pool-only rule
manualReview.suggestedDisposition: QA/Low footgun at most; verify against ledger entry 'finalizeAndReset revives pool without resetting phusdPerSecond / re-wiring yield' (open) — same revival-runbook surface, possible bundle.

manualReview.description: The empty-pool gate's safety silently depends on the totalStaked <-> strategy.principalOf lockstep invariant (restored by story-007 relinquishPrincipal). If any future/odd strategy leaves principalOf > 0 while totalStaked == 0 (the pre-story-007 buffer-path desync direction, now fixed), setYieldStrategy at line 246-249 SKIPS the drain ('staked == 0 must be a no-op'), revokes the old strategy's allowance (line 253) and decouples it — permanently stranding that residual client principal in the old strategy. The underwater check at line 238 does not catch it (principalOf > 0 with totalBalanceOf >= principalOf passes; and even underwater would merely revert, not strand). Today no in-repo path produces the desync; this is an assumption-dependency note for the incomplete-fix lens the run asked for, not a live bug.
manualReview.confidenceRationale: vulnerableWhen condition (principal desync) currently unreachable with shipped strategies given the story-007 fix (ledger: buffer-path desync entry is status fixed). Matches the pattern's signature set (principalOf/yieldStrategy/balance-delta) but the notVulnerableWhen mitigations hold at HEAD. Park for invariant-generator: assert principalOf == 0 whenever totalStaked == 0.

manualReview.description: QA: the story-010 gate makes the story-008 M-06 underwater guard (line 238) and the in-place drain branch (lines 247-249) effectively dead code. With totalStaked forced to 0 at line 228 and lockstep holding, the old strategy's principalOf is 0 (never underwater under strict <) and 'staked > 0' is unreachable. Harmless belt-and-suspenders, but the layered guards now obscure which one is load-bearing; future refactors could remove the wrong one. Not a vulnerability — code-quality observation only.
manualReview.confidenceRationale: Pure reachability reasoning; zero exploit content. QA at best per the quality bar — kept visible per Law 1 routing rather than silently dropped.

checkedClean.patternId: FIRST-DEPOSITOR-ATTACK / ERC4626-INFLATION (donation lens on the empty check)
checkedClean.rationale: The gate reads internal accounting (poolInfo[token].totalStaked), NOT balanceOf — direct token donations cannot flip the emptiness check in either direction. The idle sweep at lines 264-267 does use balanceOf, so a pre-set donation is swept into the new strategy, but at totalStaked == 0 that balance is purely protocol-owned buffer/dust (no user principal, no share-pricing) — no inflation or first-depositor surface. Principal-credit model, not shares: no exchange-rate special-casing at zero.

setYieldStrategy touches custody only, never rate/shares — no _updatePool needed. All share/rate mutators in the changed baseline (stake/withdraw/depositFor/phUSDPerDay/initiateMigration) settle via _updatePool first (pattern notVulnerableWhen satisfied).

finalizeAndReset fast-forwards lastRewardTime = block.timestamp (line 601) so the frozen Migrating window is never retro-accrued; _updatePool no-ops while Migrating and fast-forwards on empty pools. Pattern mitigations all present.

_updatePool remains the single accPhusdPerShare writer; _exitPosition zeroes the position before/with the pending mint so batchMigrate-then-userMigrate (or repeats) cannot double-mint (amt == 0 second pass).
